newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's AAPT considers share issue-paper.
newsitem.headline: Australia's AAPT considers share issue-paper.

text.p: AAP Telecommunications Pty Ltd (AAPT) was considering a share market listing as one way of raising funds for infrastructure development and acquisitions, The Australian newspaper said on Wednesday.

AAPT chief executive Larry Williams told the newspaper that the company had A$470 million of projects under consideration once the local telecommunications market was fully deregulated from July 1 this year.
The newspaper said the float could raise up to A$400 million, with other options being an equity call on current shareholders or an issue of high-yield bonds.

"As we go into deregulation we have the chance to make other investments in infrastructure and other things and we have been looking at the possibility of some kind of restructure or raising of more capital," Williams said.

AAPT, which competes with the state-owned Telstra and the privately-held Optus Communications, is 51 percent owned by the national news agency AAP Information Services, whose major shareholders are John Fairfax Holdings Ltd and The News Corp Ltd.
Singapore Telecommunications Ltd and the unlisted Todd Corp of New Zealand are the minority shareholders with 24.5 percent each.
The Australian government plans to float one third of Telstra by the end of calendar 1997, raising up to A$10 billion, while Optus is headed for a share market listing sometime in calendar 1998.
